story.opened: 24 June 1872, as the Bethnal Green Museum
story.then: According to British Listed Buildings, which reproduces the Historic England listing, the building was first put up in South Kensington in 1856-7, dismantled in 1865-7 and re-erected in Bethnal Green as a museum, opening in 1872. It took the name Museum of Childhood in 1974, then National Museum of Childhood in 1997. Londonist reported in March 2023 that the museum would reopen under the Young V&A name on 1 July 2023, after three years in the making.
story.now: The venue's own website says it is open daily and free. Its current exhibition is Inside Aardman: Wallace & Gromit and Friends, which closes on 15 November 2026.
story.vibe: Londonist describes the building as a grand barrel-vaulted hall, with a design that involved children: a Minecraft-style town square, a performance and storytelling space and a sandpit.
worth_knowing: British Listed Buildings describes the building as an early surviving prefabricated iron-framed structure.
Its first incarnation in South Kensington was nicknamed the 'Brompton Boilers', says British Listed Buildings.
Londonist says the new displays include a toy Kermit the Frog dating from the 1970s or 80s.
